entries.title: 1st house (tanu bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on identity and how you approach new situations. What approach feels authentic to you, and where would you like to experiment? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 2nd house (dhana bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on resources, values and the way you speak. Which priorities do your everyday choices reflect? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 3rd house (sahaja bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on communication, practical skills, initiative, siblings and close peers, and short journeys such as a daily commute or a weekend trip. Traditionally it also describes courage: the willingness to try something on your own. What skill or conversation deserves a little regular practice, and which brother, sister, cousin or friend would you like to stay in closer touch with? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 4th house (sukha bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on home, belonging and your private life. Traditionally it also covers your mother or main caregiver, property and land, vehicles, and the basic education that shaped you. It is the house of inner contentment (sukha). What would make your everyday surroundings feel more supportive, and is a decision about where or how you live waiting for attention? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 5th house (putra bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on creativity, play and sharing what you know. What could you make or learn simply because you enjoy it? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 6th house (ripu bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on daily work, service and routines. Which routine could be made more manageable, with help if needed? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 7th house (kalatra bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on partnerships and mutual agreements. What expectations need an honest conversation and agreement from both people? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 8th house (ayur bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on shared responsibilities, uncertainty and change. What would help you discuss a shared responsibility with clearer boundaries? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 9th house (dharma bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on learning, beliefs and broadening your outlook. Traditionally it is also the house of long-distance travel and pilgrimage, higher education, teachers and mentors, father or elders, and good fortune (bhagya). Travel abroad for study or a journey of faith is read here together with the 12th house. Which belief would you like to explore through learning, a teacher, or a journey to a new place? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 10th house (karma bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on work, responsibility and your contribution. What useful contribution would you like to practise making at work or in your community? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 11th house (labha bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on friendships, groups and shared goals. Which group or friendship aligns with goals you have chosen? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: 12th house (vyaya bhava)
entries.body: This area of the chart is used to reflect on rest, privacy and making space to reflect. Traditionally it also describes foreign lands and settling far from your birthplace, spiritual practice and liberation (moksha), sleep, retreats, charity and expenses. Questions about living or working abroad look at this house together with the 9th. What could you set aside to leave more space for rest, reflection or a long-held wish to live somewhere new? A chart is not evidence that a particular event, difficulty or relationship exists in your life.

entries.title: Mesha lagna
entries.body: Your rising sign is traditionally associated with initiative and direct action. It is the sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth, used symbolically to discuss how you approach new situations. A useful prompt is to leave space to listen before acting. It does not define who you must be.
